options: That every asset has been retired
That depreciation methods match across all categories
That every employee has an assigned asset
That the Fixed Assets subledger's balances agree with the corresponding General Ledger account balances
questions.explain: Reconciliation checks that the detailed Assets subledger and the summarized GL account balances agree for the same account and period.

questions.q: Which of these is a common timing-related cause of an apparent out-of-balance condition?
options: A category being too granular
A batch accounted in Assets but not yet transferred, or transferred but not yet posted in GL
An asset placed in service mid-year
A depreciation method using table-based rates
questions.explain: Timing gaps from the transfer-versus-post distinction (Lesson 29) are a very common and self-resolving cause of apparent discrepancies.

questions.q: How can a manual GL entry break reconciliation?
options: It cannot; manual GL entries always match Assets automatically
It automatically triggers a mass retirement
It only affects tax books, never corporate books
It changes a GL account balance without a corresponding transaction existing in Assets
questions.explain: A manual journal entry made directly in GL against a fixed-asset account, without a matching Assets transaction, breaks reconciliation because Assets has no record of that change.

questions.q: How can incorrect account mapping cause a reconciliation problem?
options: It cannot; account mapping has no effect on reconciliation
It only affects depreciation calculation, never account balances
It automatically triggers an impairment review
A category book default pointing at the wrong GL account can cause correctly generated entries to land in the wrong place
questions.explain: If a category book's default account is wrong, Assets creates technically correct-looking entries that post to the wrong account, which can look like an imbalance on the intended account.

questions.q: Why is reconciliation performed every period rather than once at implementation?
options: Because reconciliation is only legally required once per company
Because Oracle Fusion Assets deletes reconciliation data after one period
Because reconciliation automatically fixes itself after the first time it's run
Because new transactions occur every period, and catching small discrepancies early keeps them easy to trace
questions.explain: Reconciliation is a recurring discipline because new transactions and potential discrepancies arise every period; catching them early keeps corrections manageable.
